name: Stedica LMS
author: Stedica

sections.description:
Stedica LMS turns a WordPress site into a full training platform, with no external
service required.

For learners
Course catalog and self-enrolment, a course player with resume, progress tracking and
drip-released lessons, eight quiz types, certificates, leaderboards and achievements.

For instructors
A drag-and-drop course builder (lessons and topics: text, video, audio, document, SCORM,
H5P, quiz, assignment), a reusable question bank, a grading queue with a visual rubric
grid, a weighted gradebook, and per-learner and per-course progress with CSV export.

For administrators
Roles and capabilities, white-label branding, editable categories and levels, and an
audit log covering 27 action types.

Selling courses
Link a WooCommerce product to a course: the buyer is enrolled on payment and access is
revoked on refund. No external service and no subscription required.

Standards
SCORM 1.2 and 2004 import and runtime, with resume and HTTP Range media streaming.

License

Stedica LMS is distributed under the GNU General Public License. The plugin’s own code is
GPL-3.0-or-later.

It bundles third-party components under their own compatible licences, and two of them are
worth naming because they are stricter than the plugin’s own: the Freemius SDK in
vendor/freemius/ is GPL-3.0-only, and dompdf’s rendering library in vendor/dompdf/ is
LGPL-2.1. Taken as a whole, therefore, this distribution is effectively GPL-3.0 without the
“or later” option, because one of its components does not offer it.

Both LICENSE (GPLv3, the licence this plugin is under) and LICENSE-GPL-2.0.txt (included
because WordPress itself is GPLv2-or-later and the directory asks for a compatible licence)
ship in the package. GPLv3 is compatible with that requirement.

External services

This plugin connects to one external service, and only for licensing.

Freemius

Freemius handles licensing, the free trial and update delivery for the optional paid
add-on, Stedica LMS Premium. The licensing SDK is bundled in this plugin.

Nothing is sent until you choose to send it. On a fresh install the plugin runs in
anonymous mode: no request is made to Freemius and no data leaves your site. Requests
begin only when you opt in to Freemius’ service, start the free trial, or activate a
licence key — each of which is an explicit action you take.

Once you have opted in, the following is sent to Freemius:

  • when you opt in, start a trial or activate a licence: your site URL, the email address
    and name of the WordPress user performing the action, and the WordPress, PHP and plugin
    versions
  • when checking for updates to the paid add-on, and when validating a licence: your site
    URL and the installed plugin version

No learner data, course content, grades or quiz results are ever sent.

If you never opt in, the plugin remains fully functional and contacts nothing. The paid
add-on is the only thing that requires it.

Service provided by Freemius, Inc.
Terms of Service: https://freemius.com/terms/
Privacy Policy: https://freemius.com/privacy/

Security

Authorization is enforced server-side on every REST route and every admin screen —
hiding a menu item is never treated as access control. Learner-owned resources are
ownership-checked to prevent enumeration by id. Quiz answer keys never leave the
server. Protected files (SCORM assets, submissions, certificates) are served through a
PHP proxy that derives authorization from the request path, because a SCORM package’s
relative sub-resource requests cannot carry a token. Grades are clamped server-side.
Secrets are masked in every API response, and are encrypted at rest when the PHP
OpenSSL extension is available (it is on virtually all hosts; without it they are stored
unencrypted and only the masking applies).

Shortcodes

For learners: [stedica_my_courses], [stedica_catalog], [stedica_course_player],
[stedica_leaderboard], [stedica_certificates], [stedica_discussions],
[stedica_achievements]

Stedica LMS Premium, a separate add-on, adds [stedica_live_sessions],
[stedica_my_skills], [stedica_learning_paths] and [stedica_membership]. They are
listed here so you know what exists, not offered by this plugin — this package does not
contain them and does not register them.

For staff: [stedica_my_group] shows a group leader their members’ progress, and
[stedica_instructor] gives an instructor their grading queue. Both are safe to put on an
ordinary page — each shows only what the person viewing it is entitled to see, and a
visitor with no such role sees a plain explanation rather than an error.

Every surface is also a block — search “Stedica” in the inserter — and an Elementor
widget, found under a Stedica LMS category with a dropdown for which surface to show.
All three render through the same code, so they behave identically.
sections.installation:
1. Upload the plugin through Plugins → Add New → Upload Plugin, or extract into
    wp-content/plugins/.
  2. Activate. Tables, roles and upload directories are created automatically.
  3. Create a page containing [stedica_catalog] and another containing
    [stedica_course_player], then point Stedica LMS → Settings at both so links and
    emails resolve.
  4. To sell courses, set Stedica LMS → Settings → Commerce provider to WooCommerce and
    install WooCommerce if it is not already there. It defaults to None, and until it is
    set the course-to-product field does not appear on a product and no order grants
    access. Courses can of course be free, or enrolled by an administrator, with no
    provider set at all.

Certificates are rendered as PDF by dompdf, which ships inside this plugin. There is
nothing to install and no external service involved. If the library cannot be loaded —
a source checkout with no dependencies installed, for instance — certificates fall back
to printable HTML and every other feature is unaffected.
sections.faq:
Does uninstalling delete my courses?

No. Data is preserved unless you explicitly tick “Remove all data on uninstall” in
Settings before removing the plugin.

Do I need WooCommerce?

Only to sell courses. Edit a WooCommerce product and pick the course it grants from
the Stedica LMS panel; enrolment happens when the order completes, and entitlement is
always checked server-side. Refunds and cancellations revoke that access again.

What is not included?

LTI and xAPI are not implemented and are not planned. The LTI topic type is retired in
the course builder, and a course still holding one is flagged as needing replacement. H5P
is supported as an embed rather than a bundled runtime. Selling runs
through WooCommerce; there is no native card checkout in this plugin. There is no PWA
support. The plugin ships a translation template (languages/stedica-lms.pot) but no
translations.

These features are not in this plugin and are not disabled versions of anything here —
AI assistance, instructor-led sessions with seats and waitlists, competency frameworks,
multi-course learning paths, native Stripe checkout with subscriptions and coupons,
outbound webhooks, cohort analytics with at-risk scoring, and the append-only completion
register with recertification and CEU credits. They are a separate paid add-on, and the
code for them is absent from this download rather than switched off.
sections.changelog:
Older releases are in changelog.txt, which ships inside the plugin: WordPress.org
truncates this section, so only the most recent releases are repeated here.

2.7.3

  • Nothing in this package changed. It is renumbered so the pair ships as one version,
    which is checked on every build. The paid add-on’s 2.7.3 is where this release is: two
    of its queries now hand their table name to WordPress to quote, finishing what 2.7.2
    started in the database layer. There is nothing to do here.

2.7.2

  • Internal: the database layer no longer builds queries by pasting table names into
    them.     Every table and column name is now handed to WordPress to quote, the same way
    values always have been. Nothing you can see changes, and this is not a security fix:
    those names have only ever come from a fixed list inside the plugin, never from anything
    a visitor or an administrator can type. It is one less way for a future change to go
    wrong, and a test now fails the build if one slips back in.

2.7.1

  • Fixed: a certificate that failed to generate never came back. Generation happens in
    the background, and every failure ended in giving up silently — so a learner’s
    certificate could be missing for good, with only a line in the error log to say why. It
    now tries twice more, five minutes apart, except for the two conditions that waiting
    cannot change: a missing PDF library and a deleted certificate.
  • Fixed: an erasure request could be outlived by the certificate it was erasing. A
    queued render is now cancelled before the record is de-identified, and a render already
    running refuses a de-identified certificate. No learner’s name was ever written by this —
    a certificate for a deleted account renders with the name blank — but it could leave a
    stray file behind.
  • Fixed: deleting a course left its version history and group assignments behind. Both
    now go with it, from every route that deletes a course.
  • Fixed: orphaned SCORM packages were swept once and then never again. The sweep was a
    one-time repair gated on an option; it now runs daily.
  • Fixed: uninstalling left two options in the database.
  • The log line for a failed certificate write now states the cause it measured instead of
    naming two it had not checked.

2.7.0

  • Nothing changes in this plugin on its own. It supplies what the paid add-on’s new
    screens need: the site’s currency for the admin screens, a login link the group
    registration page can return somebody from, and the labels that page is built out of.
    If you do not use the add-on there is nothing here for you, and nothing to do.

2.6.0

  • New: Previous and Next in the course player. There was no way forward from a topic —
    only “Mark complete” and then a badge — and for quizzes, assignments and SCORM packages
    the action bar was empty, because those finish through their own submission flow. The
    navigation names where it goes, and never leads into a lesson that is not available yet.
  • Moving between topics now puts focus on the new title, so keyboard and screen-reader
    users are told the page has changed.
  • New: a certificate can be emailed with its PDF attached. The email itself was always
    sent on issue; the attachment is a new setting on the Settings screen — “Attach the
    certificate PDF to the completion email” — off by default, because turning it on changes
    the size of every certificate email your site sends.
  • Fixed: the admin home screen introduced the plugin twice and printed its version
    twice, once in the banner and once in a panel below it.

screenshots.caption:
The course player a learner sees: lesson and topic structure on the left, the topic
itself on the right, and progress saved as they go.

The course builder. Lessons and topics are dragged into order; each topic is text,
video, audio, a document, SCORM, H5P, a quiz or an assignment.
Every course at a glance, with how many learners are active on each.
The course catalogue on the front end, built from a shortcode or a block.
Enrolling learners one at a time or in bulk, with progress and access for each.
The dashboard, which is also where a new site starts.
